full_judgment:
"It is true that record of right indicates certain right of certain parties but that right is certainly dependent on some material evidence, oral and documentary so as to establish title in favour of persons who claim under the said record of right. The presumption of correctness as to CS record of right is not certainly available with regard to the State Acquisition Khatians. There is no presumption of correctness in respect of the State Acquisition Khatians as it is to be found in case of CS Khatians in pursuance of the provision under section 103-B of the Bengal Tenancy Act." 

 "The presumption of the CS Khatian under section 103(B) of the Bengal Tenancy Act is that every entry in a record of rights finally published shall be the evidence of the matter referred to in such entry and shall be presumed to be correct until it is proved to he incorrect. Reference may be made in this regard to the case of Akrab Ali and others vs Zahiruddin Kari and others, 30 DLR (SC) 81." 

 27. The trial Court found that earlier the plaintiffs filed objection case under section 30 of the Bengal Tenancy Act in respect of plot Nos. 2934 and 3042 of CS khatian No. 678 which was rejected. This finding is a total misreading of documentary evidence. Records show that the said objection case was filed in respect of plot Nos. 3443 and 3450 of CS khatian No. 280. Therefore, this finding, which is wrong on the face of the records, does not assist the defendants.
